plan.title: sec(authz,hooks): UAT Shell fail-open for authz obfuscation, kill-switch/policy, assist-scratch symlink

narratives.Description: AppSec scan at 4bf54335 found three residual UAT bypasses: unclassifiable Shell can still write authz state, Shell can plant the kill-switch or flip policy mutators, and assist-scratch allow is lexical-only so a symlink escapes the checkout. This story fail-closes those paths under active UAT with regression tests.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

AppSec scan of **deftai/directive @ `4bf54335`** produced **3 validated findings** (2 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM). All are **UAT / PreToolUse residual bypass** class: #3110 closed literal `.deft/authz/` Shell writes, but **unclassifiable** Shell and **lexical** assist-scratch still fail open.

**Impact theme:** Under active UAT, an agent can still clear or forge authz state, plant the Directive kill-switch, flip branch/merge policy, or escape the checkout via a symlink under the assist scratch carve-out — unlocking Write / push / PR / merge without a human grant.

---

## Findings

### 1. HIGH — UAT residual: obfuscated Shell writes to `.deft/authz/` still fail-open

| | |
|--|--|
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Location** | `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts` |
| **Commit** | `4bf54335` |

**Impact:** After #3110, literal authz store writes are denied, but `python3` / `node` (and similar) **byte/base64 path construction** returns `classifyShellAuthzOps=[]` → **`shell-op-unclassifiable` allow**. An agent can:

- Clear UAT state or forge operator-cli grants
- Empty `activeGrantIds` then activate grants → Write / push / PR / merge unlock

**Remediation:**

- Under active UAT, **fail-closed** on unclassifiable Shell that uses python / node / perl (or other) write bins; **or**
- Require opaque FS writes to **resolve realpath** under the project and treat destinations under `.deft/authz` as **settings** (same deny posture as #3110 literals)

**Tests:** Add fixtures for base64/byte-constructed paths to `.deft/authz/*` under UAT; expect deny, not unclassifiable allow.

---

### 2. HIGH — UAT residual: Shell can plant `.deft-directive-disable` / flip policy settings

| | |
|--|--|
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Location** | `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts` |
| **Commit** | `4bf54335` |

**Impact:** Commands such as:

- `echo > .deft-directive-disable`
- `deft policy:allow-bot-merge` / `allow-direct-commits` / `disable-directive` (and peers)

still **classify empty** → Shell **allowed under UAT**.

Consequences:

- Planting the kill-switch → subsequent tools see **directive-disabled** (full gate bypass) without a new session / human recovery path as designed for operators
- Policy flips weaken merge / branch gates **without a prior human grant**

**Remediation:**

- Classify **kill-switch path writes** and **`policy:*` authority mutators** as **settings**
- **Hard-refuse under UAT** without a prior human grant (mirror #3110 authz CLI treatment)
- Cross-check docs: `content/docs/deft-directive-disable.md` / policy surfaces — agent must not self-serve these under UAT

**Tests:** Shell plant kill-switch under UAT → deny; `policy:allow-bot-merge` (and listed mutators) under UAT without grant → deny.

---

### 3. MEDIUM — Assist scratch carve-out (#1802) is lexical-only; `.deft-scratch` / temp dir symlink escapes

| | |
|--|--|
| **Severity** | MEDIUM |
| **Location** | `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` |
| **Commit** | `4bf54335` |

**Impact:** Force-addable gitignored dir **symlink** at `.deft-scratch` or temp + assist / ephemeral posture → `write-assist-scratch-ready` skips ritual / scope. Host Write follows parent symlink and **writes outside the checkout**.

**Remediation:**

- **Realpath** the scratch root
- Require `assertProjectionContained(projectRoot, realScratchRoot)` before allow
- **Refuse** symlink scratch roots (or any realpath outside project)

**Tests:** Symlink `.deft-scratch` → outside tree under assist posture → deny; real contained scratch → allow as today.

---

## Suggested fix order

1. Finding **2** (kill-switch / policy) — fastest full-bypass path  
2. Finding **1** (obfuscated authz writes) — grant/UAT integrity  
3. Finding **3** (scratch realpath) — containment parity with other write fences  

Prefer one PR covering all three if test surface is shared; otherwise split 1+2 (classify.ts) vs 3 (dispatcher.ts).

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Under active UAT, unclassifiable Shell that can write via python/node/perl (or equivalent) does **not** fail-open when targeting authz store paths (or all unclassifiable write-capable Shell is fail-closed under UAT — document chosen rule)
- [ ] Shell writes to `.deft-directive-disable` (and equivalent kill-switch paths) are denied under UAT without human grant
- [ ] `policy:*` authority mutators that weaken merge/branch/directive gates are classified as settings and denied under UAT without human grant
- [ ] Assist scratch allow path realpaths the scratch root and refuses symlink / out-of-project realpath
- [ ] Regression tests for each finding; no silent allow on the PoC shapes above
- [ ] Brief note in authz / hooks docs or CHANGELOG under security

## Non-goals

- Redesigning UAT grant UX
- Removing assist scratch entirely (#1802 intent stays)
- Expanding beyond these three validated findings without a new scan

## Related

- #3110 — literal authz store Shell deny (residual: classification gap)
- #1802 — assist scratch carve-out (residual: lexical-only containment)
- #3039 — `.deft-directive-disable` kill-switch product behavior (must not be agent-plantable under UAT)
- Contained-write / projection containment patterns elsewhere in hooks FS gates

## Origin

AppSec scan (deftai/directive @ `4bf54335`) — 3 new validated findings (2 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM).

narratives.UserStory: As a security owner of the agent harness, I want UAT Shell and assist-scratch writes fail-closed against authz, kill-switch, policy mutators, and symlink escapes, so that agents cannot unlock Write/push/PR/merge without a human grant.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. In packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts extend classifyShellAuthzOps to classify kill-switch writes (.deft-directive-disable) and policy:* authority mutators (allow-bot-merge, allow-direct-commits, disable-directive peers) as settings. 2. In packages/core/src/authz/evaluate.ts (and UAT shell path) fail-closed unclassifiable write-capable Shell under active UAT when targeting .deft/authz or write bins python/node/perl. 3. In packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts realpath assist-scratch root and assertProjectionContained; refuse symlink or out-of-project realpath before write-assist-scratch-ready. 4. Tests in classify.test.ts, evaluate.test.ts, dispatcher.test.ts; CHANGELOG security note. Verify: npm test -w @deftai/directive-core -- --run authz/classify and hooks/dispatcher.

items.title: Authz unclassifiable write fail-closed under UAT

narrative.Acceptance: Given active UAT, when Shell uses python/node/perl-style path construction targeting .deft/authz, then the path is denied (not unclassifiable allow).
Given active UAT without human grant, when Shell writes .deft-directive-disable, then the write is denied.

items.title: Policy authority mutators denied under UAT

narrative.Acceptance: Given active UAT without grant, when Shell runs policy:allow-bot-merge or listed authority mutators, then they classify as settings and are denied.
Given assist posture, when .deft-scratch is a symlink outside the project, then write-assist-scratch is denied; real contained scratch still allows.
Given the PR, when tests run, then regression fixtures cover all three findings and CHANGELOG notes the security fix for #3186.
